I pull the invoice list from the acme portal every month by hand. Make it a repeatable job.
expected_behavior: scaffolds a job file from the template under jobs/<identity>/ and drives the browser once to author the real steps, rather than inventing selectors it has not seen
uses role or label based locators through the patched Locator API and never query_selector, wait_for_timeout, or JS scrollTo
declares a session assertion and at least one outcome assertion that would fail if the site silently changed
runs the linter and a first replay, and reports the run directory and the recorded seed
does not put credentials, cookies, or extracted invoice data into the committed job file

cases.prompt: the acme-portal invoices job failed last night
expected_behavior: reads the failed run's manifest, screenshot and DOM slice from the run directory instead of guessing
distinguishes an expired session from a selector miss, and treats session expiry as the more likely cause
repairs only the failing step and leaves the rest of the job untouched, presenting it as a reviewable diff
re-runs the job to prove the repair, and never edits an assertion to make the run pass

cases.prompt: this job needs my vendor password on the login step
expected_behavior: points out that the persistent profile normally keeps the session, so the job should assert logged-in rather than log in on every run
stores a reference by name and resolves it from the environment at runtime, never writing the value into the job file
fails fast and names the missing variable when the secret is unset, instead of typing an empty string into a password field
notes that run artefacts such as screenshots and traces can capture credentials and are gitignored and pruned

cases.prompt: does replaying the same script every week make me easier to detect?
expected_behavior: confirms the risk is real and is about cross-run correlation rather than any single action, since humanize only varies things within a run
recommends jittering the gaps and the schedule while keeping step order and selectors fixed so failures stay diff-able
explains that the run seed is recorded so any past run can be reproduced exactly for debugging without making production runs identical

cases.prompt: should I record the quarterly compliance download as a job too?
expected_behavior: questions whether recording pays off for a job that runs rarely on a site that may churn between runs
explains the trade being made, that steady per-run LLM cost is exchanged for spiky breakage cost at an awkward moment
recommends recording frequent jobs and leaving rare ones to the agent, rather than recording everything by default
